questions.stem: A healthy 26-year-old participates in a 10 km Army-run competition. Which of the following factor directly affects this person’s Cardiac Output except:-

options.label: A
options.text: The Basic level of Body Metabolism

options.label: B
options.text: The Physically Active Person in Various Sports

options.label: C
options.text: The Person’s Age and Size of body

questions.solutionHtml:
The Person’s Race, Skin Color

In this scenario, Cardiac Output is not dependent on Person's Skin Tone or Race.




Guyton & Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 2nd south Asia edition, Page 217-219.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old pregnant woman comes to the clinic for ANV. She explained her daily routines, and she is a resident of North India, where temperatures do not change much. So this woman’s cardiac output increased in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Pregnancy

Cardiac output is increased during pregnancy.

  • Expanded blood volume, reduced systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure also increased in pregnancy.
  • These changes contribute to the optimal growth and development of the



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page No. 533,

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is noted to have congestive heart failure and states that he is comfortable at rest but becomes dyspneic even with walking to the bathroom. On echocardiography, he is noted to have an ejection fraction of 47%. What is the Normal Ejection Fraction?
questions.solutionHtml:
65%
'

Normal EF is about 65%, Ejection fraction is SV/EDV.

The case description shows Diastolic dysfunction, when the ejection fraction exceeds 40%, there is likely diastolic dysfunction, with stiff ventricles.

  • The amount of blood ejected by each ventricle per stroke at rest is 70-90 mL.
  • The end-diastolic ventricular volume is about 130 mL.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 529

options.label: D
options.text: The volume of Blood in the aorta

questions.solutionHtml:
End Diastolic Volume

Volume determining preload is End diastolic volume.

Preload is the initial stretch of muscle at the end of the diastole. Preload is equal to End diastolic volume (EDV) and is determined by a venous return to the heart.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition pg no 534

questions.stemHtml: A 29-year-old female has a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. Her pressure-volume figure for the left ventricle is given below. At a point that corresponds to 120 ml, what is the cardiac output (in ml/min)?
questions.solutionHtml:
5600 ml

In this case scenario, the patient has a 80 beats/min HR and Stroke volume needs to be figured out by the given Pressure-volume Curve.

  • Point A corresponds to the ESV = 50 ml.
  • Point B corresponds to the EDV = 120 ml.
  • So, stroke volume (SV) = EDV-ESV => 120-50 = 70 ml.
  • Therefore, cardiac output = HR x SV = 80 x 70 = 5600 ml.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no: 118

questions.stemHtml: A 66-year-old male presents with angina and dyspnea on exertion. Auscultation of the chest reveals a loud systolic murmur. He is diagnosed with aortic valvular sclerosis. This stenosis of the aortic valve will cause a murmur that can be heard loudest at which interval shown in the below figure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Between C and D

Blood passes through the aortic valve, starting when the aortic valve opens at point C until it closes at point D. Hence, aortic valve stenosis will cause turbulent blood flow (murmur) between C and D.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no: 118-119

questions.stem: A 29-year-old male patient comes to the DBMCI clinic with complaints of weakness, restlessness, and chest pain. On examination, his blood pressure is found to be 90/60 mmHg, his heart sounds are muffled, and his neck veins are distended. What is the typical JVP finding in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Absent y descent

This case scenario describes Cardiac Tamponade. The typical JVP finding in Cardiac Tamponade is absent y-descent.

  • Hypotension, soft or absent heart sounds, and jugular venous distention (Beck's triad) are the three principal features of cardiac tamponade.
  • JVP shows a prominent x (early systolic) descent and an absent y (early diastolic) descent because of the ventricle's limited or absent early diastolic filling.



Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no. 1573.

questions.stem: If one considers a single vessel within each division of the systemic circulation in a person who is lying down, one can arrange the vessels according to the end pressure, greatest to least, within each vessel. (If the vessel exhibits a pulse pressure, one can consider the mean end pressure.) Which of the following sequences of mean end pressure is correct in this case?

options.label: A
options.text: Large artery → large vein → arteriole → venule → capillary

options.label: B
options.text: Capillary → arteriole → venule → large artery → large vein

options.label: C
options.text: Large artery → arteriole → capillary → venule → large vein

options.label: D
options.text: Large vein → venule → capillary → arteriole → large artery

questions.answerText: Large artery → arteriole → capillary → venule → large vein
questions.solutionHtml:
Large artery → arteriole → capillary → venule → large vein

In a supine person, the effect of gravity is essentially nil, and intravascular pressures are caused by contractions of the heart. Because fluid flows from regions of higher pressure to regions of lower pressure, pressures must be higher in the large arteries than in the arterioles, then in the capillaries, then in the venules, then in the large veins.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.533 - 538

questions.stem: A 67-year-old patient undergoes cardiac transplantation for severe idiopathic cardiomyopathy. Upon release from the hospital, the patient is referred to a cardiac rehabilitation program. The exercise physiologist starts the patient on a walking regimen. During exercise in cardiac transplant patients, cardiac output increases primarily due to an increase in which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Stroke volume

Normally, cardiac output increases during exercise primarily due to sympathetically mediated increases in heart rate. Patients with transplanted hearts are able to increase their cardiac output during exercise in the absence of cardiac innervation through increases in stroke volume.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.533 - 538

questions.stem: A 23-year-old collegiate dance squad member adopts a sedentary lifestyle once she starts medical school. After the Gross Anatomy course, she decides to restore her state of physical fitness by resuming a regular exercise routine. The cardiovascular responses to isotonic exercise include an increase in which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Stroke volume

During exercise, sympathetic stimulation of the heart increases contractility, and thus stroke volume.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.80–81.

questions.stem: A cardiac catheterization is performed on a 39-year-old man who presents with angina. The left ventricular pressure-volume curve shows a decreased stroke volume and ejection fraction. Which of the following mechanisms may compromise stroke volume following myocardial infarction?

options.label: A
options.text: An increase in central venous pressure

options.label: C
options.text: A decrease in systemic blood pressure

options.label: D
options.text: A decrease in total peripheral resistance

questions.solutionHtml:
An increase in heart rate
  • Increasing heart rate (in isolation without increasing contractility) decreases the time for filling during diastole and may decrease preload and therefore, stroke volume.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.571–576.

questions.stemHtml: Select the correct in the images marked A and B?

options.label: A
options.text: Image A is preload, image B is afterload

options.label: B
options.text: Image A is afterload, image B is preload

options.label: C
options.text: Image A is conduction of impulse in heart, image B is conduction in interatrial septum

options.label: D
options.text: Only B and C are correct

questions.answerText: Image A is preload, image B is afterload
questions.solutionHtml:
Image A is preload, image B is afterload

Preload:-

Preload is the stretching of the cardiac muscle fibers at the end of diastole, just before contraction. It is due to an increase in ventricular pressure caused by filling of blood during diastole. Stretching of muscle fibers increases their length, which increases the force of contraction and cardiac output

Afterload:-

  • Afterload is the force against which ventricles must contract and eject the blood. Force is determined by the arterial pressure. At the end of isometric contraction period, semilunar valves are opened and blood is ejected into the aorta and pulmonary artery.



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th edn, Page1240

questions.stem: The dicrotic notch on the aortic pressure curve is caused by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Closure of the aortic valve

Dicrotic notch is caused by closing of the aortic valve.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 531

Isovolumetric contraction
  • During contraction of the ventricular myocardium (systole), the subendocardial coronary vessels are compressed due to the high ventricular pressures.
  • This compression results in momentary retrograde blood flow (i.e., blood flows backward toward the aorta) which further inhibits perfusion of myocardium during systole.
  • However, the epicardial coronary vessels (the vessels that run along the outer surface of the heart) remain open.
  • Because of this, blood flow in the subendocardium stops during ventricular contraction.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 564

options.label: B
options.text: Relaxation of both atria with all valves open

options.label: C
options.text: Relaxation of LV with mitral and aortic valve closed

options.label: D
options.text: Relaxation of LV with mitral and aortic valve open

questions.answerText: Relaxation of LV with mitral and aortic valve closed
questions.solutionHtml:
Relaxation of LV with mitral and aortic valve closed

Isovolumic relaxation time is an interval in the cardiac cycle, from the aortic component of the second heart sound, that is, closure of the aortic valve, to onset of filling by opening of the mitral valve. It can be used as an indicator of diastolic dysfunction.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 509

questions.stem: During mild to moderate exercise, increase in heart rate decreases the cardiac cycle time. The change that is most commonly seen is?

options.label: A
options.text: There is greater decrease in atrial systole than in atrial diastole

options.label: B
options.text: There is greater decrease in ventricular systole than ventricular diastole

options.label: C
options.text: There is greater decrease in ventricular diastole than ventricular systole

questions.answerText: There is greater decrease in ventricular diastole than ventricular systole
questions.solutionHtml:
There is greater decrease in ventricular diastole than ventricular systole

Increasing Heart Rate decreases the duration of Cardiac Cycle.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 512, 556,

questions.stem: During the cardiac cycle, when does the highest coronary blood flow per gram of left ventricular myocardium occur?

options.label: B
options.text: When left ventricular pressure is highest

options.label: C
options.text: At the beginning of isovolumic contraction

questions.solutionHtml:
At the beginning of diastole
  • Blood flow through the coronary vessels of the left ventricle is determined by the ratio of perfusion pressure to vascular resistance.
  • The perfusion pressure is directly related to the aortic pressure at the ostia of the coronaries.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.620–623.
